"''Yes, you do.|Mae-ho Aniseya and Indara|audio=IndaraMae-Attackme-LostFound.flac|{{Acolyte|Lost / Found}}}} '''Indara''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] who joined the [[Jedi Order]] as a [[Jedi Initiate|youngling]] during the [[High Republic Era]]. As a [[Padawan]], she [[Jedi training|trained]] under her [[Indara's Jedi Master|Jedi Master's]] tutelage before later attaining the rank of [[Jedi Knight]] around [[161 BBY]]. Around the same [[Standard year|year]], Indara was trapped in the [[mines of Seswenna]] during the [[Farlingan Collapse]]. Afterward, to recover from the traumatizing experience, she served as a [[Jedi archivist]] in the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]]'s [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]]. Around [[160 BBY]], the [[Jedi High Council]] sent Indara to bring [[Jedi Master]] [[Vernestra Rwoh]]—who was traveling [[the galaxy]] as a [[Wayseeker]]—back to Coruscant. After Indara met Rwoh on the planet [[Cerifisis]] and helped the Jedi Master [[Second attack on the Strafes|defeat]] the [[Strafes]] [[pirate]]s [[Attacks on Norna|plaguing]] the world, the pair returned to the [[Jedi temple|Jedi Temple]]. Rwoh and Indara were tasked with [[Mission to Thelj|escorting]] [[Senator]] [[Jakob Garn]] to Coruscant, who had agreed to provide information on the [[Investigation into the production of 47 lightsaber nullifiers|production]] of [[47 lightsaber nullifier|lightsaber nullifier]] [[weapon]]s. The pair's attempt to extract him from the planet [[Thelj]] was unsuccessful, prompting them to continue their search for the [[Florinda Jackard|scientist]] working on the nullifiers by visiting the planets [[Hynestia Prime|Hynestia]], [[Ingae]], and [[Ruathi]]. On Ruathi, Indara [[Fight day|fought]] [[gheriol]] creatures in a [[Kliva's arena|fighting arena]], having been kidnapped by underlings working for the [[Arms dealer|weapons dealer]] [[Nilsson Summach]]. After Rwoh and Yorrick rescued her, the trio fled the planet and visited the [[Deva's asteroid|hideout]] of Rwoh's former acquaintance, [[Deva Lompop]]. Begrudgingly, Lompop gave the group information on the [[scientist]] Florinda Jackard, who had been working for Summach to create the lightsaber nullifiers. Indara, Rwoh, and Yorrick's [[Mission to Pinara|efforts]] to take Jackard into custody on the planet [[Pinara]] proved unsuccessful. Continuing their pursuit, they [[Mission to Septra|confronted]] Jackard and Summach in [[Nilsson Summach's private laboratory|Summach's private laboratory]] on the planet [[Septra]]. On Septra, Summach's assistant, [[Grizela]], killed her boss for his incompetence during a confrontation between Summach and Rwoh. After the incident, Grizela and Jackard were brought to Coruscant to face justice for their roles in the nullifiers' production. Upon her return, Indara submitted a request to the Jedi Council to become a Wayseeker, wanting to follow in Rwoh's footsteps. By [[148 BBY]], Indara had become a Jedi Master and was training a Padawan, [[Torbin]]. Often commanding an authoritative presence, the Jedi Master was skilled in several forms of combat, including [[Force power|wielding]] [[the Force]] to protect herself and others. In 148 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], she was [[Mission to Brendok|present]] on the planet [[Brendok]] [[Brendok four|with]] the Jedi Master [[Kelnacca]], the Jedi Knight [[Sol]], and Torbin to discover if a [[vergence]] of the Force had regenerated life on the world following the [[Great Hyperspace Disaster]]. While there, she and Sol tested the [[twin]] [[Aniseya family|sisters]] [[Verosha Aniseya|Verosha "Osha"]] and [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae-ho "Mae" Aniseya]] to be potential Padawans after discovering them within a [[Brendok coven|coven]] of [[witch]]es led by [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Aniseya]]. When Mae-ho tried to prevent Verosha from leaving with the [[Jedi]], Sol rescued her from the [[fire]] that happened afterward, bringing her into the Jedi Order as his Padawan afterward when the Jedi—including Indara—departed the world. At some point after leaving Brendok, Torbin completed his Jedi training under Indara, eventually ascending to the rank of Jedi Master. Around [[138 BBY]], Indara suggested to the Jedi High Council that Osha's training be ended, though the latter ultimately left the Order on her own. Meanwhile, Mae-ho [[Mae's quest|sought revenge]] against Indara and the other three Jedi who had been on Brendok for perceived wrongs, though the Jedi had assumed Mae-ho had [[Death|perished]] in the Brendok fire in 148 BBY. In [[132 BBY]], Indara fought Mae—now a [[Sith assassin]]—on the planet [[Ueda]] in a [[Indara's murder|skirmish]] in [[Lomi Usqi Noodle Shop]]. The pair engaged in an extended spar, with the Jedi Master defending herself using the Force as Mae-ho used her [[Mae's knives|knives]] to attack. However, Indara was ultimately killed by Mae-ho when the [[assassin]] stabbed her, as the Jedi had been distracted by acting to save the [[noodle]] [[restaurant]]'s [[Bartender|barkeep]], [[Cabuck]], from one of Mae's [[Dagger|knives]]. Following this, the Jedi Knight [[Yord Fandar]] and his Padawan, [[Tasi Lowa]], brought Verosha in as a suspect in the murder. However, they ultimately cleared her of suspicion after [[Skirmish on Olega|discovering]] Mae-ho still lived and had been involved in Torbin's death on the planet [[Olega]]. Afterward, the Jedi continued investigating Indara and Torbin's murders and displayed their [[hologram]]s in the Coruscant Jedi Temple. Meanwhile, Mae-ho [[Mission to Khofar|continued]] her quest and sought to fight Kelnacca on the planet [[Khofar]] next, though her master, a [[Sith]] she knew as the [[Merchant|trader]] [[The Stranger|Qimir]], ultimately killed the [[Wookiee]] instead. In the aftermath of the investigation, Rwoh blamed Indara, Torbin, and Kelnacca's deaths on Sol following his [[Duel on Brendok|death]] at Verosha's hands. Rwoh further insisted Sol was a rogue Jedi who had murdered his colleagues to prevent the truth of their confrontation with the witches on Brendok years before from coming to light, leaving on the official record that Indara and her fellows had conspired to hide the truth—and while true that the group had not told the entire truth, neither did Sol kill his colleagues. ==Biography== ===Jedi training=== {{Quote|My master's last words to me before I became a Jedi Knight were to chastise me for my unkempt robes. So you are correct. I do not have the fond memories of my master that you have of yours.|Indara to Vernestra Rwoh, about her Jedi Master|audio=Indara1-Wayseeker.flac|}} The [[human]] [[Gender|female]] Indara was [[Reproduction|born]] around [[186 BBY]] during the [[High Republic Era]]. [[Standard day|Days]] after her birth, she was left at the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]], joining the [[Jedi Order]] as an [[Jedi Initiate|infant]]. As she grew up, Indara retained no memories of her life before becoming a [[Jedi]] and considered Coruscant her [[homeworld]]. At some point, she participated in a [[Gathering]] on the planet [[Ilum]] in which she collected a [[kyber crystal]] for her [[Indara's lightsaber|lightsaber]] in the world's [[Crystal Cave]].''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' specifies that Indara gathered her [[kyber crystal]] from [[Ilum]], an event that {{TCW|The Gathering (episode)}} defines as a [[Gathering]], which were held in the [[planet]]'s [[Crystal Cave]]. Later, Indara [[Jedi training|trained]] as a Jedi [[Padawan]] under the tutelage of a [[Indara's Jedi Master|Jedi Master]]. As his student, she traveled [[the galaxy]] with her [[Jedi Master]], learning about various cultures and their fighting forms and saving endangered [[Book|tomes]]. [[File:JediVector-CGSWG.png|thumb|right|300px|Indara flew a Jedi Vector (pictured) during her time as a Jedi, though preferred other methods of transport.]] When traveling, Indara's Master often chose utilitarian [[transport]] methods, such as [[shuttle]]s and [[Planet hopper|hopper]] [[Starship|spacecraft]], for their missions. However, Indara also occasionally flew a [[Jedi Vector]]—a swift and nimble [[Interceptor|vessel]] designed specifically for Jedi use''[[The High Republic: The Rising Storm]]''—though she disliked using the [[starfighter]]s outside [[Space warfare|combat]]. Indara's Master regularly berated and belittled her during their training, including during their [[lightsaber duel]]ing sessions and when the former felt his apprentice looked unkempt. To please her Master, Indara spent significantly more time sparring and testing her skills through drills in training rooms than her peers did. On at least one occasion as a Padawan, Indara fought [[pirate]]s. During her time as a Padawan, Indara and her Master traveled extensively, including to the [[Lake Country]] of the planet''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' [[Naboo]] and the [[water]]falls of the planet''[[Star Wars: The High Republic Character Encyclopedia]]'' [[Dalna]]. Other locations they visited also had natural formations that Indara felt were impressive, including the shifting sands on the astronomical [[Leonit]] and the large [[tree cow]]s on the celestial body Holpern. Around [[163 BBY]], Indara became aware of the [[Jedi Annexation Act]], a piece of legislation that [[Galactic Republic]] [[Senator]] [[Jakob Garn]] and his allies were proposing in the Galactic Senate. At the time, Indara was focused on her research concerning the cultural relevance of [[shishi tea]] to the [[Kessarine]] population of the world [[Eriadu]], having been asked for the research by a [[Unidentified Jedi Master (shishi tea)|Jedi Master]] embarking on a [[diplomat]]ic mission. As a result, she did not pay much attention to other Jedi's discussions on the piece of legislation. Indara and her Master continued to share a tense relationship until Indara was [[Knighting Ceremony|knighted]] and rose to the rank of [[Jedi Knight]] around [[161 BBY]].The events of ''[[The Acolyte: Wayseeker]]'' take place around [[160 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:WayseekerDate|here]]. ''The Acolyte: Wayseeker'' specifies that the [[Farlingan Collapse]] and Indara's [[Knighting Ceremony|knighting]] took place one [[Standard year|year]] before the novel's events, equating to [[161 BBY]]. ''The Acolyte: Wayseeker'' also dates the attempted passing of the [[Jedi Annexation Act]] to three years prior to the novel's start, equating to around [[163 BBY]]. ===Farlingan Collapse=== {{Quote|I was in the mines on Seswenna during the Farlingan Collapse. You may not have heard of it. I was there with four other Jedi. I was the only one who survived. It took them a week to find me. We went down there because the miners had been complaining about the work conditions and a lack of safety, holding up production. The Senate asked the Order to get involved, since the mines were crucial to the economies of a few different planets. We were supposed to be there to help keep them safe. Instead we were pinned behind some rubble. The other Jedi died instantly, but my leg was just pinned. And the Force … well, it wasn't much help.|Indara, reminiscing about the Farlingan Collapse|audio=Indara2-Wayseeker.flac|}} [[File:Senate_seal.svg|thumb|left|250px|At the request of the Galactic Senate (seal pictured), Indara and four other Jedi were sent to Seswenna to mediate with miners.]] Around the same [[Standard year|year]], Indara, her former Jedi Master, and three other Jedi were sent to the planet''[[The High Republic: Defy the Storm]]'' [[Seswenna]] on a [[Mission to Seswenna|mission]]. At the request of the [[Galactic Senate]], the group attempted to mediate with the [[Miner|workers]] in the [[mines of Seswenna]]—who had been complaining about their work conditions and lack of safety—to ensure production would resume, as the [[Mining|mines]] were heavily entwined with the economies of a few planets. However, though the five Jedi attempted to keep the workers safe, during a visit to the mines, they were buried deep beneath Seswenna's surface by rubble in an event that became known as the [[Farlingan Collapse]]. The four Jedi with Indara [[Death|died]] instantly, though she survived with only her [[Limb|leg]] pinned. Stuck in stifling darkness, Indara listened to the cries of the miners dying around her, growing fainter by the [[Local day|day]]. Though Indara was able to ease her suffering by drinking from a nearby puddle, she otherwise waited for rescue while enduring excruciating pain, only alleviated by unconsciousness and attempts at [[meditation]]. While trapped, Indara envisioned that a [[Unidentified Kessurian male|Kessurian male]] wearing [[Jedi apparel|temple robes]] had comforted her. Eventually, she was rescued by a [[Unidentified droid crew|droid crew]] after a [[Standard week|week]] had passed. She spent a few weeks in a [[bacta tank]] to heal upon returning to Coruscant, missing the remembrance ceremonies for her Jedi colleagues. Upon waking up, Indara had lost confidence in her abilities as a Jedi due to the mental trauma of the incident, which included her Master's abrupt passing. Though she asked after the [[Kessurian]] who had been in the mines with her, she was informed that no individuals of that [[species]] had been present. After Indara submitted a request to be reassigned to Coruscant's [[Jedi temple|Jedi Temple]], the request was approved, and she was offered the position of a [[Jedi archivist]] until she felt ready to return to the mission roster. ===Jedi archivist=== {{Quote|I've studied it extensively. I've even written several analyses of the initial Jedi response in the aftermath of the incident on Valo. I've mostly been interested in the initial Emergences and—''"
"''I only ask because it seems as though the Order was quick to forget the failures of our leadership during that time. And since you're young, I wasn't sure how much you'd been exposed to, even as an archivist.''"
"''Yes, well, I happen to have written my first treatise on the actions of the Order during the Nihil conflict and how the casualties could have been avoided at key junctures.|Indara and Vernestra Rwoh, about the Nihil conflict|audio=Indara3-Wayseeker.flac|}} [[File:TrymantEmergence-2021THRA1.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Indara took particular interest in studying the Emergences of the Great Hyperspace Disaster (Emergence pictured).]] As an archivist, Indara answered to a [[Indara's supervisor|supervisor]] while working in the Jedi Archives, often using the Archives' terminals to complete research requests. Though lauded by other archivists for her skills, Indara regularly brushed off their praise, assuming every kind word from her colleagues was made out of pity. Indara spent time researching the [[Nihil conflict]], in which the [[Nihil]] marauders fought against the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order. Though particularly interested in the initial [[Emergences]] of the [[Great Hyperspace Disaster]] of [[232 BBY]], the Jedi Knight also wrote several analyses on the initial Jedi response to the [[Valo Atrocity|attack]] on the [[Valo Republic Fair|Republic Fair]] on the planet [[Valo]]. At another point, Indara drafted a treatise on how the Jedi Order might have avoided more casualties during the Nihil conflict by taking actions at various key junctures in the multi-year struggle. The Jedi Knight learned about Jedi Master [[Vernestra Rwoh]] and her exploits against the Nihil and in other conflicts afterward, such as the [[Darnaburny Civil War]]. Indara also studied the treatises of [[Imri Cantaros]], a renowned Jedi [[philosopher]] whom Rwoh had trained. After researching the Nihil conflict, Indara also studied the [[Great Hyperspace Rush]] of [[383 BBY]]. Though several assignments were announced during her year as an archivist, Indara shied away from adding herself to the mission roster, unsure of her skills and preferring to stay in the Jedi Archives. During this time, she researched the [[Shani]] species, finding the conflicting narratives about the species' history intriguing. Ahead of an upcoming celebration on the planet [[Tevu]], Indara began researching a [[battle on Tevu]] that had taken place when Jedi Master [[Yaddle]] had been a Padawan. The archivist was concerned with the redactions and contradictions in the Jedi Archives' reports of the event and resolved to speak with Yaddle about her findings later, as the latter had been involved in the conflict. ===Finding a Jedi Master=== ====A new directive==== {{Quote|You want me to go find a Jedi Master? I… wouldn't it be easier to just send her a message to return?''"
"''The first thing you should know about Vernestra Rwoh is that she is not easily swayed from her path. We have a matter that needs her personal attention, and the timing is urgent.|Indara and Oppo Rancisis|audio=Indara4-Wayseeker.flac|}} [[File:TempleDistrict-LostFound.png|thumb|left|300px|Indara was tasked with bringing Vernestra Rwoh back to Coruscant's Jedi Temple (pictured).]] Around [[160 BBY]], several recently reported usages of a [[47 lightsaber nullifier|lightsaber nullifier]] worried the [[Jedi High Council]] due to the risk it posed to Jedi. By this point, the Council's previous attempts to send Jedi to investigate the [[weapon]] had failed, having only received scattered reports of the device being used throughout the [[galaxy]] since its unveiling at the Valo Republic Fair nearly eighty years before. The Jedi Masters decided to assign Rwoh to [[Investigation into the production of 47 lightsaber nullifiers|track]] down the manufacturer of the nullifiers, tasking Indara with bringing the Jedi Master—who was currently traveling the galaxy as a [[Wayseeker]]—back to Coruscant's Jedi Temple. When Indara was summoned to meet the [[Jedi Council|Jedi High Council]], she briefly spoke with Yaddle on her way to the [[Jedi Council Chamber|Council Chamber]], anxiously wondering why she had been called to a meeting. Expecting to be assigned a research request, Indara was surprised to learn her objective was to bring Rwoh to Coruscant. Jedi Master [[Oppo Rancisis]] indicated that Rwoh was not easily contactable. As the Council needed her to handle a specific, [[time]]-sensitive issue, the best option was to send an [[emissary]]. Indara was then dismissed and immediately sent to board her assigned Jedi Vector. Though displeased with having to fly the vessel, preferring a more utilitarian craft, Indara departed the Jedi Temple in the Vector and jumped to [[hyperspace]]. After noting that Rwoh's last known location was the planet [[Cerifisis]], she [[Star map|mapped]] the [[Hyperspace route|route]] to the world and identified two potential pit-stop locations: the planets [[Haileap]] and [[Eiram]]. Knowing Rwoh's first assignment as a Jedi Knight had been Haileap, Indara chose to travel to the former, wanting to visit a place the Jedi Master had once resided. Meanwhile, as Indara traveled, Yaddle informed Rwoh via transmission that a Jedi would escort her to Coruscant. ====Pit stop and pirate skirmish==== {{Quote|Master Vernestra Rwoh. I am Jedi Knight Indara. And I am here to escort you back to Coruscant at the request of the Jedi Council. You must come with me.|Indara to Vernestra Rwoh|audio=Indara5-Wayseeker.flac|}} Upon landing on Haileap, Indara took a brief stroll around the [[Port Haileap]] outpost. At the insistence of the [[Ugnaught]] woman [[Orna]], Indara visited [[Kimnol's Gambling Hall]], noticing the latter's worried expression as she tried to convince the Jedi to go inside. Indara surveyed her surroundings from a table, spotting the [[Dashon|human man]] arguing with a [[Florinda Jackard|human woman]], who accused him of cheating her. As they spoke, the [[Gigoran]] [[Hinra]] entered the establishment, wielding a large [[repeating blaster]]. Indara was shocked at seeing such a large weapon—one generally meant for a [[landspeeder]]—and powered on her lightsaber to [[Lightsaber combat|parry]] the [[blaster]] bolts Hinra began spraying the [[Cantina|tavern]] with. When Hinra aimed at Indara, she sliced the [[barrel]] of his repeating blaster with her [[lightsaber]], and [[Force push]]ed him out the door. With appreciation, the Ugnaught offered her a mug of a foamy beverage and a [[Foodstuff|pastry]] as thanks. Afterward, Indara departed Haileap and continued toward Cerifsis. The [[Arms dealer|Weapons dealer]] [[Nilsson Summach]] met with his subordinates aboard his [[Nilsson Summach's pleasure cruiser|pleasure cruiser]], discussing the outcome of Indara's involvement in their affairs in Haileap. [[File:J-6_ATOC.png|thumb|right|250px|On Cerifsis, Rwoh's droid J-6 (pictured) took her to meet the Jedi Master.]] After arriving on Cerifsis, Indara met Rwoh's [[droid]], [[J-6]], who escorted her to where Rwoh was meditating. Indara introduced herself to the Jedi Master, recounting the Jedi Council's request for Rwoh to return to Coruscant. Rwoh was surprised by Indara's relative inexperience, having expected the Jedi Council to choose a stalwart colleague from her younger days to convince her to return. Sensing Indara's nervousness, Rwoh decided that Indara should help her defeat the pirates [[Attacks on Norna|plaguing]] Cerifsis—the [[Strafes]]—before they departed the world. Indara and Rwoh boarded a [[hauler]] headed toward the [[Strafes' hideout]], planning to [[Second attack on the Strafes|attack]] them there. While in the vehicle, Indara reflected on her initial meeting with Rwoh, finding the older woman unlikable, though impressive. Upon noticing the younger Jedi Knight sweating, Rwoh taught Indara how to [[Unidentified body temperature regulation power|regulate]] her body [[temperature]] with [[the Force]], though the latter felt that the former's tone was patronizing. After the Strafes stopped the hauler, the Jedi exited the vehicle and began combating the pirates. The pair eventually went down a hallway and found the pirates' leader, a [[Unidentified Toydarian pirate|Toydarian]]. Indara powered up her lightsaber, prompting the Toydarian to activate a lightsaber nullifier via a bangle on his wrist, rendering both her and [[Vernestra Rwoh's purple-bladed lightsaber|Rwoh's lightsabers]] useless. The Jedi pair began using the Force as their weapon, subduing the pirates with objects such as their [[lightsaber hilt]]s, dishes, [[pipe]]s, and wire. Once [[Unidentified security team|Cerifsis's security team]] arrived to handle the situation's cleanup, Indara, Rwoh, and J-6 departed the planet aboard Rwoh's [[VKCE-7100x Starcutter|ship]], the ''[[Cantaros]]''. Aboard, Rwoh informed Indara about the lightsaber nullifier the [[Toydarian]] had wielded against them on Cerifsis. ===A dramatic report=== {{Quote|You sent me because you knew my inexperience would provoke Master Rwoh to action. She returned with me to the Temple because you made her curious.''"
"''Vernestra has always loved a challenge, and you bear the unique distinction of being one of the few Jedi Knights who would not buckle under her withering gaze. You were the perfect choice to provoke her to action. Besides, the Council has let you hide in the archives for the past year. Have you never wondered why that is?''"
"''I haven't been ''hiding''. I've been busy. I had to do the treatise on the Nihil conflict, and then on the Hyperspace Rush, and then there was the new research… you know this.''"
"''I know that you are a highly capable Jedi who has buried herself in the past after a tragedy. I know that you have never requested to be placed on the mission roster despite your colleagues urging you to. And I know that you have never fully dealt with the trauma you lived through on Seswenna.''"
"''That's… that's not fair. Or true. I just… I've been busy. It's only been a year, not ten.|Indara and Yaddle|audio=Indara6-Wayseeker.flac|}} [[File:Yaddle-ConceptArt.jpg|thumb|left|230px|Indara confronted Yaddle (pictured) in her living quarters after returning to the Temple.]] Upon arriving on Coruscant, Indara promptly visited [[Master Yaddle's living quarters|Yaddle's quarters]] to confront the Jedi Master. Indara expressed dissatisfaction at being chosen to retrieve Rwoh for reasons other than her competency, as the Jedi Master had only returned with her due to her curiosity. Yaddle countered, indicating that Indara was the perfect choice to prompt Rwoh into action, as her talents were not best used hiding in the [[Jedi Archives|archives]], and she also needed to begin healing from the trauma of the Farlingan Collapse. Afterward, Indara and Yaddle left the latter's quarters to attend Rwoh's audience with the Council, which was also open for Jedi spectators. Rwoh extolled her adventures as a Wayseeker to the waiting crowd of Jedi, impressing those present, including Indara. Having surmised that the Council would not act on the threat of the lightsaber nullifiers, Rwoh publicly demonstrated using one of the devices she had acquired on Cerifsis during a mock duel with Yaddle. Most Jedi were then summarily dismissed from the room, leaving only the Council, Rwoh, and Indara. In their brief discussion, Indara expressed her belief that knowledge of the lightsaber nullifiers should not be kept a secret so that the Jedi might be prepared. Afterward, in Yaddle's quarters, Yaddle relayed more information on the Council's past efforts to track down lightsaber nullifiers. Yaddle then assigned Indara and Rwoh to meet with Garn, who had been rumored to be connected with a weapons dealer selling the nullifiers nearly fifteen years before. The Jedi Master told Indara and Rwoh that Garn had recently expressed a willingness to cooperate with the Republic, with what he knew about the weapons dealer, in exchange for safety. Though both Jedi were displeased to work with each other again, they departed without voicing a complaint. ===Tracking a weapon=== ====Escorting a senator==== {{Quote|Now, since you're the archivist, tell me what you found out about Garn that might be most useful.''"
"''So, judging from his past and the way he uses his knowledge of relevant laws, this is not an honest request from him. I don't think he actually plans on turning himself in. He's escaped prosecution for a number of crimes and still holds a favored position on senatorial committees.''"
"''Do you think this is a distraction of sorts?''"
"''I looked a bit deeper into the Jedi Annexation Act that Garn sponsored. It never truly had the support it needed to pass, but it kicked up enough fuss that people stopped asking questions about Garn's investment in some very unsavory corporations. The man is the master of the misdirect. I suspect there is some piece of information that hasn't yet come to light—a bargaining chip hidden up his sleeve, so to speak. I suspect that once we get him safely to Coruscant, he has some scheme he'll put into action. The senator has spent an entire lifetime avoiding consequences, and I don't think that kind of person gives up easily.|Vernestra Rwoh and Indara|audio=Indara7-Wayseeker.flac|}} [[File:VernestraRwoh-tattoos.png|thumb|right|270px|Aboard the ''Cantaros'', Indara and Vernestra Rwoh discussed the significance of the latter's facial tatoos (pictured).]] Indara and Rwoh [[Mission to Thelj|departed]] for the planet [[Thelj]] aboard the ''Cantaros'', with J-6 [[pilot]]ing. In hyperspace, Indara researched the Jedi Annexation Act that Garn had supported years before to understand the senator she was about to meet. The Jedi Knight was shocked by the plentiful documentation of Garn's alleged misconduct in several incidents throughout his Senate tenure. Demotivated by the information, she set down her [[datapad]] and left her [[Indara's quarters|quarters]] to meet with Rwoh. The Jedi pair discussed Garn's past while enjoying [[lompop liqueur]] in the ''Cantatos''{{'}} galley. Indara and Rwoh then discussed the latter's practice of shaving her head and the significance of the [[Mirialan]]'s [[tattoo]]s. In return, Indara informed Rwoh of the trauma of the Farlingan Collapse, which was why she had been serving as an [[archivist]] on Coruscant for the last year. Afterward, the pair briefly discussed Garn before heading to [[sleep]]. Upon landing on Thelj, the pair disembarked, discussing the planet's relative state of dilapidation after the world was left behind by their main benefactors, the [[Graf family]]. The two Jedi boarded a [[train]], eventually making their way to [[Senator Garn's office|Garn's office]] in the [[Unidentified city (Thelj)|city]] center. After receiving word that Garn still intended to meet with them, the [[Jakob Garn's droid|droid]] escorted Indara and Rwoh into a waiting room. Shortly after, Garn arrived and welcomed them, inviting them to stay and talk with him. When Rwoh pushed for them to depart, he briefly apologized to her before diving to the ground as [[Unidentified human assassin 1|two]] [[Unidentified human assassin 2|gunmen]] stormed the room. Indara and Rwoh ignited their lightsabers, only for their weapons to flicker out when the attackers used a lightsaber nullifier. Indara's group of Jedi also used a ship on Brendok, which featured comms technology, a portable conference table with a [[holoprojector]], and a Jedi testing screen. The four Jedi on Brendok also had access to two [[Jedi outland speeder bike]]s for scouting the world's dense forests. [[File:Indara-JSW.png|thumb|left|170px|Indara wielded her lightsaber against Mae-ho Aniseya on Ueda.]] Years later, on Ueda, she wore multi-layered ivory-colored Jedi [[robe]]s featuring delicate pleating{{SW|url=news/dressing-the-acolyte-costumes-feature|text=Dressing ''The Acolyte'': The Stranger and an Assassin Hunt the Jedi of the High Republic — Updated|date=2024-06-03}} and a [[Synthleather|synth-leather]] chestpiece with a hook-and-bar spiral closure. The Jedi Master also donned a brown utility belt with a gold-colored buckle and pleated brown [[boot]]s. Her undertunic featured a slight ribbing pattern, while her overtunic was made of rougher, more structured material. She also donned a billowing brown cloak whose flowy nature could help obscure her stance and confound opponents. The Jedi Master owned a silver-colored comlink. Indara wielded a lightsaber with a verdant green blade, built with a kyber crystal from Ilum. It had a gold-and-silver [[hilt]] with a coppery finish, an emitter shroud denoting her cautious demeanor, and [[power cell]] charge indicators. She kept the weapon attached to her belt to symbolize the Jedi's role as guardians of peace in the galaxy.{{Databank|indara-s-lightsaber|Indara's lightsaber}} ==Behind the scenes== ===Milestones=== {{Quote|Having the opportunity to work on a ''Star Wars'' production was something I don't think I ever imagined that I would do. What I love about the approach that Leslye did in telling this story, is that we see it from two perspectives. Anything has multiple perspectives. As a human being I'm interested in that.|Carrie-Anne Moss|{{Getty|url=thewaltdisneystudios/allaccess#!asset/cfbb67xmwfbh74fst5h84hvb|text=THE ACOLYTE Production Brief FINAL 5-01-24|date=2024-05-28}}}} [[File:Indara-Filming.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Filming for ''The Acolyte'']] Indara first appeared in "[[Lost / Found]]," the first episode of the live-action [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which aired on [[June 4]], [[2024]].{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-teaser-poster|text=''The Acolyte'' Teaser Poster, Premiere Date Revealed|date=2024-03-18}} She was visually depicted in a [[Celebration Europe (2023)|Celebration Europe]]-exclusive trailer{{CelebrationTrailer|''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]''|Celebration Europe (2023)}} released during the [[Lucasfilm]] Studio Showcase on [[April 7]], [[2023]]. [[Carrie-Anne Moss]]'s casting for the role was revealed in a [[StarWars.com]] article the [[April 8|following day]].{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-lucasfilm-studio-showcase|text=SWCE 2023: 11 Highlights from Lucasfilm's Studio Showcase|date=2023-04-08}} Indara was first identified by name in a StarWars.com article on March 18, 2024, that announced ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} first publicly available trailer and the series' premiere date. A [[May 4]], 2024, StarWars.com article revealing ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} final trailer and poster art indicated that Torbin was Indara's Padawan.{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-trailer|text=Darkness Rises in ''The Acolyte'' Final Trailer and Key Art|date=2024-05-04|oldversion=20240504212207}} However, the information had been removed from the article by [[May 7]].{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-trailer|text=Darkness Rises in ''The Acolyte'' Final Trailer and Key Art|date=2024-05-04}} Torbin was later confirmed to have been Indara's Padawan in events set prior to ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} main storyline that were depicted in the third episode of the series, "[[Destiny (The Acolyte)|Destiny]]," which was released on [[June 11]], 2024.{{DisneyPlus|subdomain=press|url=news/next-on-disney-plus-june-2024|text=Next on Disney+: June 2024}} Indara's name was misspelled as "Inara" in the [[Star Wars Insider 131|131st issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine, in the "[[Launchpad]]" section.{{InsiderCite|231|Launchpad}} The issue was published on [[April 29]], [[2025]].{{TitanComics|url=m/179-star-wars-insider-231|text=Star Wars Insider #231}} ===Filming=== {{Quote|It was unusual, like I wasn't used to that. Because I'd been in other big stuff but like when you walk out of your trailer and go to set you have to cover your costume. And I would forget, and so someone would run after me and throw a robe over me and I'd be like 'oh I'll remember tomorrow' and then, I would forget.|Carrie-Anne Moss, on filming ''The Acolyte'' as Indara|audio=CarrieAnneMoss-IndaraInterview.flac|{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@JimmyKimmelLive|name=Jimmy Kimmel Live|video=SGL6L69k-3g|text=Carrie-Anne Moss on Star Wars: The Acolyte, Doing Fight Scenes & Embarrassing Old Baywatch Clip|date=2024-06-13}}}} Indara's stunt double, [[Katie McDonnell]], practiced lightsaber choreography with Moss for the role,{{Instagram|username=bycarrieannemoss|url=p/C71yZlypjBq|name=[[Carrie-Anne Moss]]|date=2024-06-05|quote=Practice practice practice @katiemcdonnell @officialacolyte|archiveurl=https://archive.is/oNS0H|archivefile=File:CarrieAnneMoss-LightsaberPractice-Instagram.png}} with the latter copying the movements of the former. As part of her role, McDonnell—portraying Indara—worked on scenes for the Ueda duel, remarking after the show's release that Moss had excelled with that fight's choreography{{Instagram|username=katiemcdonnell|url=p/C9C1Tiyt2qo|name=[[Katie McDonnell]]|date=2024-07-05|quote=@bycarrieannemoss smashed the fight choreography… 🙌🏼 I smashed the wall. 😅|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/uHaNl}} and commended the latter's dedication.{{Instagram|username=katiemcdonnell|url=s/aGlnaGxpZ2h0OjE4MjYyNDU3MDMyMjE0Mjkz?story_media_id=3385789038379382365&igsh=dmxxYWhvamdueTJi|name=[[Katie McDonnell]]|date=2024-06-24|quote=@bycarrieannemoss killed it in this scene! So much dedication fully paid off!|nobackup=1}} {{C|Story originally by Katie McDonnell and reposted by [[Lu Junchang]]; original story now inaccessible}} Meanwhile, as stunt double, she had been tossed into the noodle establishment's wall. On Brendok, McDonnell also completed the scene in which Indara tackled Kelnacca by putting him in a leg grab. The scene was rehearsed for a long time to get the grab and subsequent fall done right.{{InsiderCite|230|Kelnacca Kaos}} Like the rest of ''The Acolyte'', Indara's scenes were filmed on practical sets and limited usage of CGI to honor Headland's vision.{{YouTube|video=9Cc3aHsZ1iY|text="The Acolyte" Interview with Amandla Stenberg & Leslye Headland|channel=@majorfilmevents|name=majorfilmevents|date=2024-06-02}} Moss spent around three weeks training for the role leading up to the series' production in action and stunt combat preparation, finding the process extremely physically exhausting due to the short timeframe.{{WebCite|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a60985164/carrie-anne-moss-the-acolyte-interview|text=Carrie-Anne Moss on 'The Acolyte' Episode 1 Twist, 'The Matrix,' More|author=[https://www.esquire.com/author/15317/brady-langmann Brady Langmann]|date=2024-06-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Esquire (magazine)|''Esquire'']]|archivedate=20240605140412}} Despite her initial struggles, Moss became much more comfortable with the physical aspect of the role by the last week of her training. Ultimately, filming for all of Indara's scenes lasted three months.{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/features/star-wars-acolyte-carrie-anne-moss-interview-jedi-master-indara|text=The Acolyte: Carrie-Anne Moss Talks Jedi Master Indara, Star Wars Spirituality, And Lightsaber Duels|author=[https://www.empireonline.com/author/ben-tavis Ben Travis]|date=2024-05-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20240604164342}} Similar to her co-star, the first fight sequence Stenberg and her stunt double{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-amandla-stenberg|text=The Acolyte's Amandla Stenberg on Playing Twins, the Sith, and ''Star Wars'' — Updated|date=2024-06-10}}—[[Kellina Rutherford]]{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-stunts-and-fights|text=Fight Like a Jedi: Inside The Acolyte's Stunt Sequences and Martial Arts Action}}—learned for ''The Acolyte'' was also the noodle shop duel against Indara. [[File:IndaraLightsaberTraining-Instagram.gif|thumb|left|300px|Carrie-Anne Moss and Katie McDonnell practiced Indara's choreography together.]] Moss indicated that one of the primary reasons she wanted to portray Indara was the opening fight scene of the series on Ueda, as she had not done acting work with that level of choreography in a long time and considered it a deep responsibility.{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@Comicbook|name=Comicbook.com|video=YPlbUwULr-o|text=The Acolyte Cast Picks Their Lightsabers! Star Wars: The Acolyte Cast Interview!|date=2024-05-28}} She considered the scene to be the favorite one she had filmed for the show, despite how tiring the training for it had been.{{SWYouTube|7Dju63U24m0|The Acolyte | Crafting the Combat | Streaming Tuesday on Disney+}} Moss was passionate about making sure she used her lightsaber properly while filming, wanting to do it exactly right. She would practice with a baton in her hotel to prepare, and participated in reshoots until the scene was perfect, considering it one of the most stressful parts of the performance. In an interview, Moss noted that while traveling to and from set, she was required to cover her costume to maintain confidentiality. The actor found it an unusual practice and often forgot to do so, resulting in a production staff member chasing after her to bring a robe on some occasions. The scene where Indara tackled Kelnacca to the ground was filmed in a warehouse at Arborfield Film Studios, which was an old military base in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]]. Meanwhile, the campfire scene with the Brendok Jedi—including Indara—was filmed at [[Pinewood Studios]]{{Lucasfilm|url=news/lucasfilm-on-location-the-acolyte|text=Lucasfilm on Location: ''The Acolyte''}} in the United Kingdom,{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/the-acolyte-a-journey-to-the-filming-locations-part-2-uk|text=The Acolyte: A journey to the filming locations Part 2: UK|author=[[Sander de Lange]]|work=[https://www.fanthatracks.com Fantha Tracks]|archivedate=20250304030611}} from [[December 8]] to [[December 10|10]], 2022.''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' Other scenes on Brendok were shot in [[Wikipedia:Wales|Wales]]. The entrance to the Brendok fortress was shot at Upper Neuadd Reservoir and Dam in Wales, and interior shots were filmed at [[Shinfield Studios]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]].{{Lucasfilm|url=news/julian-foddy-acolyte|text=''The Acolyte'' Visual Effects Supervisor Julian Foddy}} Interior shots of the Jedi's transport ship, as well as the interior scenes in the Lomi Usqi Noodle Shop,{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/the-acolyte-a-journey-to-the-filming-locations-part-1-madeira|text=The Acolyte: A journey to the filming locations Part 1: Madeira|author=[[Sander de Lange]]|work=[https://www.fanthatracks.com Fantha Tracks]|archivedate=20241204220147}} were also shot at Shinfield Studios. The site of the Jedi ship{{WebCite|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx92exjz98ro|text=Star Wars show swaps galaxy far, far away for Wales|author=Leston, Ryan|work=[[Wikipedia:BBC|BBC]]|archivedate=20240714093614}} and the locations where the Jedi explored and catalogued Brendok were also filmed at Upper Neuadd Reservoir. ===Portrayal=== ====Casting==== {{Quote|Oh, it was such an exciting call to get. Actually, my husband and children watch all the ''Star Wars'' shows. They're watching it, and I'm carrying a bunch of clothes upstairs to put in people's closets. My husband calls out, "You should be on one of those shows!' And literally two weeks later, I got the call.|Carrie Anne Moss, in an interview for ''The Acolyte''|}} [[File:Carrie-AnneMoss.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Carrie-Anne Moss, the actor who portrayed Indara]] Moss enjoyed the method series creator [[Leslye Headland]]'s used to create ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} story, finding multiple perspectives shown in the narrative particularly interesting. The actor was excited to be part of a ''[[Star Wars]]'' production and had not imagined doing so in the past. Though she knew ''Star Wars'' was a lore-heavy franchise, she sought to bring her character to life in her own way by staying open minded and trusting her director. She found portraying a Jedi to be "incredible,"{{SWYouTube|zotV8szyesw|The Acolyte | Creating the Acolyte | Streaming June 4 on Disney+}} honored to be part of a franchise that has impacted many people, including her family, who were excited to see the series upon its release.{{SWYouTube|RXF0IfbgpXQ|The Acolyte | Exploring Star Wars | Streaming June 4 on Disney+}} In the past, her family had often joked about her taking on a ''Star Wars'' role, with Moss noting that in one instance, they had done so, and she had gotten the call to be in ''The Acolyte'' two weeks later. One of her sons is a ''Star Wars'' fan, and she asked both him and Headland a lot of questions to feel grounded in the universe's lore.{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@HOLLYWOODINSIDERTV|name=Hollywood Insider|video=kRad-Oo5kqw|text=Carrie Anne Moss Spills Secrets on 'The Acolyte' at Hollywood Premiere|date=2024-06-02}} She immediately accepted the role upon offer wanting to pour her heart and soul into the character because of her appreciation for Headland's work. Moss felt that her fight scene had a story in it, specifically calling out Indara's "containment" as an aspect she liked, in that the character had power in her but moreso that her true power came from strict control and prowess over her abilities, rather than letting loose and wild, and to make it look effortless. The actor enjoyed her character's fierce demeanor and sense of humanity and at one point spoke to [[Pablo Hidalgo]] while preparing for the role. In an interview ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} launch premiere for cast, press, and select fans on [[May 23]], 2024, Moss expressed her hopes for fans to enjoy the journey, story, and action the series' characters would engage in.{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-premiere|text=''The Acolyte'' Launch Event Takes Hollywood|date=2024-05-24}} ====Showrunner thoughts==== {{Quote|This was a big question when we were working on the episode. To me, it was very important because it told two stories. One, that Indara, despite her being completely and utterly the consummate Jedi in this episode, I did feel it was important that she also misjudged something. If we were going to explore those themes, she couldn't just be this infallible Jedi, she also had to have something else going on with her. And I think what she did is, in the moment, in trying to sever the connection between Kelnacca and the witches, she dealt with a power that she did not understand and was unfamiliar with.|Leslye Headland, about Indara's actions in "Destiny"|}} [[File:Leslye_Headland.jpg|thumb|left|200px|''The Acolyte''{{'s}} showrunner, Leslye Headland, created Indara.]] Headland was inspired by Trinity from ''The Matrix'', who was portrayed by Moss, hence why her casting in the show was "no-brainer" as Hedland wanted the audience to see Indara as one of the most powerful Jedi in the room by perceiving her like "Trinity with a lightsaber." Moss felt hooked by Headland's vision for the show in the same way she felt connected to her projects with [[Wikipedia:Christopher Nolan|Christopher Nolan]] and [[Wikipedia:The Wachowskis|the Wachowskis]], enjoying playing a Jedi Master and training to do so, acknowledging that her role as Indara made her realize how much she loves the action genre and aims to make her part perfect.{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/news/acolyte-carrie-anne-moss-jedi-master-indara-inspired-by-trinity-exclusive|text=The Acolyte: Carrie-Anne Moss' Jedi Master Indara Is 'Very Much Inspired By Trinity' — Exclusive|author=[https://www.empireonline.com/author/ben-tavis Ben Travis]|date=2024-04-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20240407204023}} Moss has expressed that the nature of the Force was an intriguing concept, particularly how Jedi could train to use the Force as a "[[Wikipedia:Chinese martial arts|kung-fu]]" style force field within the story of a fight.{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@GMA|name=Good Morning America|link=Wikipedia:Good Morning America|video=g_VGsvd9mYc|text=Carrie-Anne Moss talks new 'Star Wars' series|date=2024-05-27}} The showrunner felt that the fast paced scenes with a lot of physical exertion made the scenes feel more visceral to the audience, stating that Moss was able to perfectly stay on-beat with her death scene. Concerning Indara's actions in "Destiny," Headland has stated that the Jedi Master did not know her actions to save Kelnacca would result in the deaths of the witches controlling him. The showrunner felt that—though Indara was otherwise depicted as a model Jedi Master—it had been important for her to misjudge at least one thing. She felt that the character felt so strongly about saving Kelnacca in the moment that she did not consider the ramifications interfering with such power could have, having only been worried about what the witches could do her colleague after the unnerving control they had displayed over Torbin previously. The showrunner also discussed the differences between Sol and Indara's views on how to proceed after the Council denied their request to take the twins to Coruscant, noting that while the former was correct in a human and fatherly aspect, the latter had been acting as a Jedi should. ====Cast commentary==== {{Quote|When I heard the first person I'd fight was Carrie-Anne Moss, I had a heart attack.|Amandla Stenberg, fighting Indara's actor|audio=AmandlaStenberg-FightingMoss.flac|}} [[File:AmandlaStenberg-SisterhoodInterview.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Amandla Stenberg felt that Carrie-Ann Moss took her under her wing while they filmed the noodle shop duel as Mae-ho and Indara, respectively.]] The actor [[Manny Jacinto]], who portrayed Qimir, felt that bringing in Moss from an iconic franchise such as ''The Matrix'' showed audiences that ''The Acolyte'' would be a new and fresh type of ''Star Wars'' not seen before.{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/star-wars-tv-shows/the-acolyte-opening-master-indara-death-explained|text=''The Acolyte'' creator breaks down Star Wars show's shocking opening: "You have to go hard, you have to say the Jedi are going to take some Ls"|author=[https://www.gamesradar.com/author/bradley-russell Bradley Russell]|date=2024-06-05|work=[[Wikipedia:GamesRadar+|''GamesRadar''+]]|archivedate=20240606025958}} [[Charlie Barnett]], Fandar's actor—agreed with Moss's statement that the noodle shop duel was one of her favorite scenes in the series. He particularly highlighted Moss's prowess of the Force in the fight sequence as Indara, joking that she was a "strong, wise Jedi." [[Amandla Stenberg]]—who portrayed Mae-ho and Verosha in ''The Acolyte''—said she nearly had a heart attack upon learning the first person she would fight in the show would be Moss. Stenberg indicated that she knew Moss had been in [[Wikipedia:The Matrix (franchise)|''The Matrix'' franchise]] portraying [[Wikipedia:Trinity (The Matrix)|Trinity]], a character Stenberg considered one of [[Wikipedia:Science fiction|science fiction's]] most powerful and intimidating characters. Despite her anxiety over their characters fighting, Stenberg also felt Moss kindly took her under her wing while they filmed Indara and Mae's scenes together.{{WebCite|url=https://decider.com/2024/06/03/amandla-stenberg-was-terrified-to-fight-carrie-anne-moss-in-new-star-wars-show-the-acolyte|text=Amandla Stenberg Was "Terrified" to Fight Carrie-Anne Moss in New Star Wars Show 'The Acolyte'|author=[https://decider.com/author/meghan-okeefe Meghan O'Keefe]|date=2024-06-03|work=[[Wikipedia:New York Post#Decider|''Decider'']]|archivedate=20240606025423}} Moss, meanwhile, stated that training for the fights needed for filming was a very special experience to share, expressing that Stenberg was dedicated to her performance. She was also was fond of her co-star [[Lee Jung-jae]]'s portrayal of Sol, finding that his acting had a lot of heart in it to make scenes feel genuine.{{SWYouTube|B0WxdRadrm8|The Acolyte | Sol of the Jedi | Streaming June 4 on Disney+}} As part of the show's promotional releases, Moss and her fellow cast members participating in an unboxing video on the official ''Star Wars'' [[Wikipedia:YouTube|YouTube]] channel for ''The Acolyte''-themed [[Hasbro]] ''[[Star Wars: The Black Series]]'' figurines of their characters.{{SWYouTube|arx7huV_X7s|The Acolyte | Cast Product Unboxing | Disney+}} Later, Moss expressed her surprise after learning ''The Acolyte'' had been canceled. However, she noted that since her character had already died in the first season, she was not as emotionally invested in the project continuing as she had not expected Indara to reappear{{WebCite|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/paultassi/2024/10/18/the-acolytes-carrie-anne-moss-gives-her-thoughts-on-its-cancellation|text=The Acolyte's Carrie-Anne Moss Gives Her Thoughts On Its Cancellation|author=[https://www.forbes.com/sites/paultassi Paul Tassi]|date=2024-10-18|work=[[Wikipedia:Forbes|''Forbes'']]|archivedate=20241026185810}} and did not spend a lot of time thinking about it not being renewed.{{YouTube|video=-XQV-NWPsRs|text=Carrie-Anne Moss Talks Die Alone, The Matrix's 25th Anniversary, The Acolyte Cancellation|channel=@comingsoon|name=ComingSoon.net|date=2024-10-22}} She also indicated surprise at fans' vitriol at her character's death, saying that she had known Indara would die upon taking the role but did not think about how it would impact fans.{{WebCite|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/carrie-anne-moss-idara-death-the-acolyte-star-wars-2025-|text=Carrie-Anne Moss didn't think her death on 'The Acolyte' would be a big deal: 'How did I miss that?'|author=[https://www.businessinsider.com/author/jason-guerrasio Jason Guerrasio]|date=2025-06-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Business Insider|''Business Insider'']]|archivedate=20250625225827}} ===Development=== ====An intentional cold open==== {{Quote|From a filmmaker perspective, I just felt like with the cold open, especially with a new story, that you just have to go hard. ''[…]'' It just has to be a moment where the emotional and the physical—meaning the fights–melt together. Carrie-Anne, not just being an action legend, is also a phenomenal actress. She was able to play all those beats within the fight as well as, of course, her death scene.|Leslye Headland|}} [[File:KillBillposter.jpg|thumb|left|215px|The martial arts ''Kill Bill'' franchise heavily influenced the choreography of Indara's fatal duel.]] The scene of Mae-ho and Indara's duel was considered an "essential entry point" into ''The Acolyte'' as a series. To this end, under the direction of production designer [[Kevin Jenkins]], production designer [[Sophie Becher]] worked in preproduction to create several illustrations of the event. In the script for "Lost / Found"'s [[Wikipedia:Cold open|cold open]], Headland described Indara's demeanor on Ueda as relaxed and controlled, similar to{{SW|url=lost-found-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Lost / Found" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 6}} the Jedi Master''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]'' [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] or the character O-Ren Ishii from the [[Wikipedia:Kill Bill: Volume 1|''Kill Bill'']] franchise, a martial arts movie series.{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/kill-bill-movie-timeline-chronological-order|text=Kill Bill Complete Timeline Explained|author=Ben Sherlock; Colin McCormick|date=2024-04-06|work=[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|''Screen Rant'']]|archivedate=20240606020840}} Alongside ''Kill Bill'' as an influence, Headland also likened Indara's demise as similar to the local inn scene in the [[Wikipedia:Shaw Brothers Studio|Shaw Brothers']] [[Wikipedia:Come Drink with Me|''Come Drink with Me'']]. Though Headland understood why some fans may have found Indara's death shocking, she indicated that it was important for the Jedi to be able to lose, making them not infallible. The showrunner felt the duel was a tradedy for Indara and a victory Mae-ho, allowing viewers to hold both concepts in their mind during the same sequence. Headland's background as a television writer inspired her decision to have Indara's death scene as a cold open.{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/the-acolyte-creator-leslye-headland-explains-shocking-premiere-opening-scene-865678|text=''The Acolyte'' creator explains that shocking premiere opening scene|author=[https://ew.com/author/dalton-ross Dalton Ross]|date=2024-06-04|archivedate=20240606030830}} The showrunner was particularly fond of the cold open to the television series [[Wikipedia:Breaking Bad|''Breaking Bad'']], and while thinking about what version of that she could put in her own show, settled on killing Moss's character to shock those who would recognize the actor and the parallels between her character Trinity in ''The Matrix''. The actor indicated that she always knew her character would die in the opening scenes of ''The Acolyte'', stating that Headland had wanted her death to impact the audience. ====Noodle shop choreography==== {{Quote|In this fight, I thought it was important to show that Mae's sort of testing Indara in her own way. She's making sure that Indara's always going to be a Jedi and that she's going to protect the innocent.|Christopher Clark Cowan aviyt Indara and Mae's Ueda duel|audio=ChristopherClarkCowan-NoodleShop.flac|}} [[File:ChristopherClarkCowan.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Christopher Clark Cowan helped design the choreography for Indara and Mae's duel.]] Action designer and second unit director [[Christopher Clark Cowan]] indicated that Mae-ho and Indara's duel intentionally depicted the assassin trying to attack Indara without a weapon first, before raising the stakes and using knives after being unable to land blows on the Jedi Master. Cowan felt that the duel scene depicted Mae-ho trying to test Indara's resolve to protect innocents throughout the fight, as the Jedi otherwise was only acting defensively. Cowan also expressed that it was important for Mae-ho to realize that Indara would always do the right thing. Cowan then noted that after Mae-ho realized Indara would stay on the defensive, she uses that to her advantage to take her out, albeit in a way she did not prefer. The unit director particularly commented on his pleasure working with Moss during filming, having been a fan of Moss in ''The Matrix''. [[Lu Junchang]], an assistant fight coordinator for ''The Acolyte'', noted that extensive wire work and Force pushes were used in the scene to set a standard for the rest of the series' fights. [[File:MossCowanFilming.jpg|thumb|left|290px|Christopher Clark Cowan, Carrie Anne Moss, and Kellina Rutherford filming the noodle shop fight]] Indara's scene on Ueda was inspired by{{SW|url=lost-found-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Lost / Found" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 7}} the film{{WebCite|url=https://www.sonyclassics.com/film/crouchingtigerhiddendragon|text=Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon | Sony Pictures Classics|work=[[Wikipedia:Sony Pictures Classics|Sony Pictures Classics]]|archivedate=20240225174110}} [[Wikipedia:Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon|''Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon'']], as both it and ''The Acolyte'' feature fast, high-flying martial arts choreography. Headland's input on the choreography was also influenced the ''Kill Bill'' franchise, and elements of that franchise were seen when Mae-ho swiftly jumped away from Indara and onto the noodle shop's second floor. The showrunner's crew worked hard to incorporate heavy elements of hand-to-hand combat and martial arts into every major fight scene, including Indara's on Ueda, while also striving to make each combat sequence in ''The Acolyte'' unique to viewers.{{SWYouTube|gBk-okerzAo|The Acolyte | Stunts | Disney+}} Each movement in the fight was planned out months prior to filming digital pre-visualization and motion capture technology over the course of a week from stunt coordinator [[Mark Ginther]]'s studio. Ginther expressed appreciation for the work Moss put in to learn the complex lightsaber and fight choreography for the noodle shop scene given the limited timeframe she had. ====Indara's duel's music==== {{Quote|…it's really primitive, but also a bit kinetic. Then, when the lightsaber is drawn, there's a harkening back to traditional ''Star Wars'' language there. And then finally, you here a theme that I call the theme of profound loss. And it happens as we watch Indara die. And it becomes a crucial theme throughout the series, and we hear it at points whenever a character is thinking about or experiencing a profound loss.|Michael Abels, about the music in Indara's duel|audio=MichaelAbels-NoodleShopThemesAcolyte.flac|{{SWYouTube|kPoBKsu9qXs|The Acolyte | Michael Abels | Disney+}}}} [[File:MichaelAbels.png|thumb|right|235px|Composer Michael Abels created the themes used in Indara's scenes on Ueda.]] Composer [[Michael Abels]], who created the musical score for ''The Acolyte'', indicated that the music in the noodle shop fight sequence was intended to have a kinetic and slightly primitive energy throughout Indara and Mae's fight. Having felt the fight's musical theming was crucial for setting the rest of ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} tone, he informed Headland that he did not wish to work on the sequence first while doing work for the series. Abels noted that when Indara drew her lightsaber in the scene, the stakes of the skirmish were raised to a new level, echoing the traditional themes of ''Star Wars'' music. The composer described the music that played when Indara died as a "theme of profound loss," which he indicated would be used in other parts of the series in the future when other characters felt or experienced the same emotions. ====''The Acolyte: Wayseeker''==== {{Quote|…and I think it's for me I wanted to say Indara, you know, like Indara—is this very closed off person—but what if she wasn't always like that? What if, in the beginning, she tried to be a little more open, and then it kinda backfired.|Justina Ireland about Indara, in an interview|audio=JustinaIreland-Indara.flac|{{Spotify|url=episode/3NKS0kSnmbAigSE1BrV5jF|text=Wayseeking with Justina Ireland}}}} Indara appeared in the novel ''[[The Acolyte: Wayseeker]]'', a tie-in book for ''The Acolyte'' written by [[Justina Ireland]] that was released on [[May 6]], 2025.{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/761123/the-acolyte-wayseeker-star-wars-by-justina-ireland|text=The Acolyte: Wayseeker (Star Wars)}} On [[December 17]], 2024,{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1869083897075831099|[[Tom Hoeler]]|date=2024-12-17|quote=Justina's story is turning out with so many lovely moments with Indara/Vernestra.|archiveurl=https://archive.is/tqNy4}} [[Random House Worlds]] Senior Editor{{WookYouTube|wBCosZCW7x8|Wookieepedia Interviews - Tom Hoeler}} [[Tom Hoeler]] teased her role in the work, mentioning that there were "many lovely moments" with Indara and Rwoh within and that he felt Ireland's work delving into Indara's mindset, past, and journey to becoming a Jedi Master was amazing.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1919393069490675950|[[Tom Hoeler]]|date=2025-05-05|quote=Ahead of tomorrow's release of #StarWars #TheAcolyte #Wayseeker here's an excerpt feat. Indara (who is a Jedi Knight in this book). Author Justina Ireland did amazing work delving into Indara's mindset, a bit of her past and her journey toward the Jedi Master we met in Acolyte.|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/PEOMI|archivefile=File:TomHoeler-DayBeforeWayseeker-Twitter.png}} As part of the teased information, Hoeler released an unattributed quote from the novel.{{Twitter|DarthInternous|status/1869083895171539168|[[Tom Hoeler]]|date=2024-12-17|quote=The briefest peek at next year's #Wayseeker: "...we are all lights, and no matter how brightly we burn, we are all chasing away at least a little of the darkness. And I want to be that person for someone, the person who pushes back the shadows just enough to make life better."|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/fh5JK|archivefile=File:TomHoeler-BriefPeekWayseeker-Twitter.png}} ''Wayseeker'' itself later revealed the speaker of the quote to be Indara. [[File:JustinaIreland.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Justina Ireland, the author of ''The Acolyte: Wayseeker'', which featured Indara]] When conceptualizing Indara's character arc for ''Wayseeker'', Ireland took notes on aspects of the Jedi Master's demeanor in ''The Acolyte'', including how tough and closed off she was. In this respect, the author wanted to write a younger Indara that was very insecure and very much an "open book." As she was writing the book, ''The Acolyte'' was canceled, thus allowing Ireland greater freedom to explore specific aspects of Indara's character. Ireland felt that Indara's master was often critical of her, something the author reflected was not brought up in conversations among the Jedi. The author felt that this strictness did not necessarily make Indara's master a bad person but still affected the woman Indara eventually became. Ireland intended for Indara to try to be more open during ''Wayseeker'', noting that the approach eventually backfired for the Jedi, thus putting the character down a path in which she would become the strict and controlled Jedi Master seen in ''The Acolyte''. The author enjoyed the idea of archivist librarians in the Jedi Order seeing more action outside of their regular duties and was particularly fond of archivists' role in preserving important historical information for their institutions. Ireland hoped that Indara's story would be continued via other media.{{Spotify|url=episode/3NKS0kSnmbAigSE1BrV5jF|text=Wayseeking with Justina Ireland}} Ireland felt that writing Rwoh's scenes in first person helped better show the Jedi Master's internal realization that she needed to shift her approach with Indara, as the latter grew to dislike her patronizing behavior. When writing, Ireland was only given the overarching plot and details for the first three episodes of ''The Acolyte''. Knowing Indara's ultimate fate in the noodle shop, Ireland sought to make the younger Indara embody the least likely characteristics of Moss, which was ultimately that of a nervous and timid librarian. Later, the author watched the rest of the episodes to get more details on the character. Ireland wanted Indara to be a foil for Rwoh, finding it amusing that a Jedi Knight would have to be sent to get a Jedi Master.{{WebCite|url=https://fullofsith.libsyn.com/fos/episode-dlxxxix-the-acolyte-wayseeker-with-justina-ireland|text=Episode DLXXXIX: The Acolyte - Wayseeker with Justina Ireland|work=[[Full of Sith Podcast]]|date=2025-05-27|format=[[Wikipedia:Podcast|Podcast]]|archivedate=20250530200542}} ===Costume development=== ====Jedi robes==== {{Quote|Knowing that Master Indara was going to be the first Jedi that you saw in ''The Acolyte'', I really wanted to still keep that essence of how we've seen them, that significant and memorable brown mission cloak. How she's hooded—I think it was a really great shot. Anyone who is a Star Wars fan, which for me is everybody on the planet, knows that that is a Jedi.|Jennifer Bryan, on Indara's costume|}} [[File:Obiwanoldguy.png|thumb|left|250px|Indara's Jedi attire was based on Obi-Wan Kenobi's from ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''.]] ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} costume designer, [[Jennifer Bryan]], created Indara's Jedi attire and other costume elements, with assistant costume designer [[Carly Griffith]] also contributing to the ensemble.{{WebCite|url=https://www.carlygriffithcostumedesigner.co.uk/the-gentlemen-2|text=Gallery 3 — Carly Griffith Costume Designer|work=[https://www.carlygriffithcostumedesigner.co.uk carlygriffithcostumedesigner.co.uk]|archivedate=20250510005828}} Bryan sought to make the Jedi Master recognizably a Jedi to anyone who saw her—both [[in-universe]] and outside of it—by having her don the classic brown Jedi robes that were first worn by Obi-Wan Kenobi in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The ivory coloring of Indara's Ueda Jedi robes beneath her cloak was inspired by [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa's]] white dress from the original trilogy. The designer felt that the scene of Indara in her hood on Ueda was particularly memorable and liked its finished result, having designed her costume by keeping in mind that the Jedi Master would be the first Jedi depicted in the series. [[File:IndaraRobesStitching-DressingAcolyte.jpg|thumb|right|270px|The leather doublet of Indara's costume featured topstitching matching the tunic beneath.]] A structured leather [[doublet]] was constructed for Moss to give her more support, using stiff material that featured topstitching matching the delicate pleating of her undertunic and the micro pleating of her boots. Aside from their stylistic qualities, Bryan created all components of Indara's costume with utility in mind to suit ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} action choreography. Moss noted that the boning in the costume injured her at some points because it restricted the movement of her back. Though the actor did not often feel the pain while in character, she often needed to recover from filming each night due to the costume's constraints. ====Lightsaber filming==== {{Quote|I decided to focus on the lightsaber ignites and steady hums. For ignites, the base sound is a remastered version of a classic lightsaber ignite. In addition, I recorded and then processed various paper tears, as well as added an explosive element to give it more weight. For the steady hums, I used Ben's original hum, but pitched it differently for different characters. I then ran the pitched hum through a plugin that added a small amount of feedback distortion, which gave the hum a slightly grittier quality.|Kimberly Patrickm on the lightsabers used in ''The Acolyte'', which included Indara's|}} [[File:IndarasLightsaber-SDCC.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Indara's lightsaber was displayed in the Lucasfilm Pavillion at San Diego Comic Con.]] According to sound designer [[Kimberly Patrick]], the sound emitted when all lightsabers used in the series ignite, including Indara's lightsaber, was customized by the VFX efforts of [[Industrial Light & Magic]] and [[Skywalker Sound]] after starting as a version of the classic lightsaber ignition sound. For the steady humming sound produced by an active lightsaber blade, Patrick used a modified version of the sound from [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's third lightsaber|Kenobi's lightsaber]] in the original trilogy, using various methods to slightly distort and alter the pitch for different characters. The Jedi Master's lightsaber was displayed alongside several others at ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} press premiere on May 23, 2024, as well as in the Lucasfilm Pavillion at [[Wikipedia:San Diego Comic Con|San Diego Comic Con]],{{SW|url=news/sdcc-2024-lucasfilm-costume-display|text=SDCC 2024: The Stranger from ''The Acolyte'' Arrives at the Lucasfilm Pavilion}} held from [[July 25]] to [[July 28]] of the same year.{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2024/07/comic-con-2024-schedule-movies-tv-panels-events-1236006770|text=Comic-Con 2024 Schedule: The Top Movie & TV Panels And Events In San Diego|author=Anthony D'Alessandro; Patrick Hipes|date=2024-07-25|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20241008060227}} Much of the center glow lighting of Indara's lightsaber was added after filming, as actors had filmed with a new, hybrid type of lightsaber not previously used in ''Star Wars'' productions. This new type of lightsaber made use of lucite hilts and embedded LED lights, brought to life by propsmaster [[Joshua Polley]] and the props manufacturing team led by [[James McKeown]]. Though Headland wished to have at least some light reflecting off characters faces in filming to have a further depth of realism, she realized that lighter props, such as the ones used in the [[prequel trilogy]], were necessary to make them usable. The showrunner personally selected the lightsaber colors for each original character in ''The Acolyte'',{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@RottenTomatoesTV|name=Rotten Tomatoes|link=Wikipedia:Rotten Tomatoes|video=hkJos35CuV0|text='The Acolyte' Cast on New Lightsabers and Droids|date=2024-05-30}} which included Indara, based on the aesthetic of what the scene needed and the character's personality. ====Lightsaber concept artwork==== {{Quote|Initially we had a different Production Designer who wanted to really explore a very different approach to the design of the sabers, as this was the height of the Republic we decided to look in to old duelling pistols and a more deliberate Baroque style as if each saber was bespoke built for the user.|Adam Burn, in his post releasing the concept artwork for Indara's lightsaber|{{ArtStation|username=adamburnart|url=artwork/8bA86Q|name=[[Adam Burn]]|text=Star Wars Acolyte: Indara Lightsaber Initial Concepts|date=2024-06-25}}}} [[File:IndarasLightsaber-AdamBurnInitialConcept.jpg|thumb|right|300px|One of Adam Burn's initial concept artworks for Indara's lightsaber]] Several initial concept artwork pieces of Indara's lightsaber was created by artist [[Adam Burn]] as one of his first projects for ''The Acolyte''. He noted that the first production designer attached to the lightsabers' creation wanted to explore a unique approach to their design, and had the artistic team look into old dueling pistoles and details from the Baroque architectural style to make each one unique for its user. One design featured an intricately carved half black and half gold hilt with an emitter shield, activation button, two variants of holster attachments, and a cerulean blue blade. A second design featured many similarities but instead added more rod-like framing around the hilt and replaced the carving with a cord-like grip section. [[File:IndarasLightsaber-AdamBurnRefinedConcept.jpg|thumb|left|300px|One of Adam Burn's refined concept artworks for Indara's lightsaber]] Burn's third lightsaber design was a curved, white marble hilt with a blue blade that illuminated from the inside when ignited, which featured gold leaf patterning and a black and gold hilt base. His last two blue-bladed concept artwork pieces featured a version of Indara's lightsaber with an almost entirely black hilt with faint gold overlay on top, while the other featured a solid white marble hilt with a gold base and latticed top detailing. Burn also released the refined concept artwork for Indara's lightsaber, noting that several details from the initial concepts had been simplified, while still keeping the "bespoke" aspects of them. Each of the refined concepts were then 3-D printed. Of the six designs the artist posted, most bore gold, silver, black, and gun metal gray coloring, with some bearing square shaped hilts and others being round. The artwork pieces each had a blue blade, either lattice work or ribbing, and some had grips or decorative carvings.{{ArtStation|username=adamburnart|url=artwork/ob4EaL|name=[[Adam Burn]]|text=Star Wars Acolyte: Indara Lightsaber Refined Concepts|date=2024-06-25}} The final version of Indara's lightsaber was a silver-and-gold round hilt with a blue blade, made in a traditional lightsaber style, albeit with a copper grip to introduce a new type of material. Prop modeler [[Jacob Clare]]—who created at least one concept illustration for Indara's lightsaber design—felt that Headland cared about the appearance of Indara's lightsaber more keenly because it was the first seen in ''The Acolyte''. Alongside his lightsaber concept pieces, Burn also created an illustration of Indara's comlinks. ====Costume and story concept art==== {{Quote|Knowing that Master Indara was going to be the first Jedi that you saw in ''The Acolyte'', I really wanted to keep that memorable brown mission cloak. How she's hooded—I think it was a really great shot. Anyone who is a ''Star Wars'' fan knows that that is a Jedi.|Eleanor Barlow, on designing Indara's concept artwork|}} [[File:IndaraCostume4-EleanorBarlow.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Concept artwork of Indara's costume, by Eleanor Barlow]] Four concept artwork pieces of Indara's costumes were created by artist [[Eleanor Barlow]]. Two featured her in light-colored Jedi robes, with one also having a brown, hooded Jedi cloak. The second pair of concept artwork pieces featured Indara in layered, yellow Jedi attire, with one having a cloak and one remaining without.{{ArtStation|username=ebarlow|url=artwork/4Noe1Y|name=[[Eleanor Barlow]]|text=Indara|date=2024-06-25}} The makeup artist [[Jeremy Woodhead]] created a colored sketch sheet of several potential makeup and hair styles for Indara. Some of the designs included [[cybernetics]], hairpieces, and decorative facial markings. Artist [[Vincent Jenkins]] created three pieces of concept art for the Brendok campfire scene, which included Indara and the other Jedi sitting together.{{Instagram|username=vincentjenkinsjnr|url=p/C_BPeG1IH7N|name=[[Vincent Jenkins]]|date=2024-08-23|quote=Concept for Star Wars "The Acolyte" #starwars #conceptart #theacolyte #art|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/v7MWd}}{{Instagram|username=vincentjenkinsjnr|url=p/C_IVODEiq5w|name=[[Vincent Jenkins]]|date=2024-08-26|quote=The Acolyte. Concept art #starwars #theacolyte #conceptart #painting #illustration|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/Hqf23}} Under the direction of Kevin Jenkins, artist [[Adam Brockbank]] created two pieces of concept artwork depicting Mae-ho standing over a dying Indara during the Ueda duel scene.{{Instagram|username=brockbankadam|url=p/C-Zq4Ugq5KN|name=[[Adam Brockbank]]|date=2024-08-08|quote=Mae reveal The Acolyte Production designer Kevin Jenkins #theacolyte #starwars #starwarsconceptart #conceptart #conceptartist|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/HWqKg}} In July 2024, more pieces of the duel scene were displayed at Lucasfilm's ''Star Wars'' booth at San Diego Comic Con,{{WebCite|url=https://mouseinfo.com/2024/07/sdcc-2024-props-and-costumes-for-the-acolyte-on-display-at-star-wars-booth|text=SDCC 2024: Props and costumes for THE ACOLYTE on display at Star Wars booth|author=Inigo, Joey|date=2024-07-24|work=[https://mouseinfo.com MouseInfo]|archivedate=20250403023105}} {{C|[[Wikipedia:San Diego Comic Con]], [[Lucasfilm]]'s ''[[Star Wars]]'' booth}} one of which was illustrated by artist [[Ferenc Norhof]].
